children.html: Knead until dough is smooth and separates from the bowl. Let it rise in a warm place for 30 minutes.

Cut tablespoonfuls of dough, round them into balls, let them rise on a floured surface for 10 minutes. Drop dumplings into rapidly boiling salted water, boil 5 minutes, turn them around with a spatula and cook another 5 minutes. Drain, pierce each with fork, sprinkle with hot butter.

Optional: Coat with fried bread crumbs.
Serve with meats and sauces.

• • 5 medium potatoes
  • • 1 cup flour
  • • 1 cup cream of wheat, regular, not precooked
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 whole eggs
  • • salt
Peel potatoes, cook in salted water, drain. Mash them, add butter, eggs, salt. Mix thoroughly, blend in flour and cream of wheat. Knead until dough is smooth and dry.
Pinch off bits of dough, roll into 2" balls. Cook in lightly salted boiling water 10-12 minutes. Serve immediately.
Serve with roast goose, pork, cabbage, sauerkraut.

• • 5 medium potatoes, boiled, cooled, peeled and diced
  • • 2 medium onions, finely chopped
  • • 5 slices ham cut in thin strips
  • • 7 pickled cucumbers, peeled, diced, squeezed dry
  • • 2 large green apples, Granny Smith, peeled, cored, diced
  • • 2/3 cup Hellmann's mayonnaise mixed with 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
  • • 2 teaspoons vinegar
  • • 2 teaspoons white wine Worcestershire sauce
  • • white pepper

Place potatoes in a large bowl, sprinkle with vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, pepper. Add onions, ham, apples. Add pickles last, making sure they are squeezed dry. Lightly toss together all ingredients. With a spatula thoroughly but carefully blend in mayonnaise/mustard mixture. Chill to blend flavors, at least several hours. To serve, spoon salad in a bowl lined with lettuce. Serve with roasts, chicken, meatloaf.

• • 1-1/2 quarts beef stock
  • • 1 lb. beef stew meat cut in 1/2" cubes
  • • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • • 2 slices bacon cut in short strips
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut in 1/2" cubes
  • • 1 tablespoon paprika
  • • 4 tablespoons flour
  • • 1/2 teaspoon each of caraway seeds, marjoram, ground nutmeg
  • • 3 cloves garlic, pressed or chopped
  • • salt and pepper

In a large saucepan combine oil, bacon and onion, brown it lightly. Add paprika, beef, pepper, caraway seeds, marjoram, nutmeg, garlic. Cover and simmer until beef is almost tender, about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding 2-3 tablespoons beef stock, just enough to keep moisture in the pan. Uncover, blend in flour, braise 5 minutes. Add potatoes, beef stock, bring to boiling. Cook over medium/low heat until potatoes and beef are tender, 15-20 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cream of chicken soup - Krém z kuřat

• • 2 quarts water
  • • 1 small chicken, 2 lbs., quartered
  • • 2 beef soup bones
  • • soup greens (carrot, celery, parsley)
  • • 1 medium onion, quartered
  • • 1/3 teaspoon ground allspice
  • • 1 egg yolk
  • • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • • salt and pepper
  • • 2 tablespoons butter and 3 tablespoons flour for the roux
Place water, chicken, bones, soup greens, onion, salt in a large saucepan. Bring to boiling. Simmer, covered, 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Remove chicken when cool, discard skin and bones, puree chicken meat. Reserve.

In a separate saucepan stir flour into melted butter and cook until bubbly and golden brown. Gradually add the broth from the chicken, bones, allspice and pepper. Cook 10 minutes over medium heat. Strain. Stir in puréed chicken. Lightly beat egg yolk and cream and blend mixture into soup. Season with salt and pepper. Heat through. Do not boil after egg yolk/cream addition.

• • 2 lbs. tripe
  • • 2 quarts chicken broth
  • • 2 carrots
  • • 1 celery root, or 4 stalks
  • • 1 medium onion, quartered
  • • 4 cloves garlic, pressed or chopped
  • • 2 tablespoons paprika
  • • 1/2 teaspoon each of marjoram, ground allspice, black pepper, ginger
  • • 3 tablespoons butter and 4 tablespoons flour for the roux
  • • salt
Most supermarkets and butchers sell tripe already cleaned and parboiled, so just rinse it well in cold water. However, if you need to start from scratch, here's how:

Clean tripe well and rinse thoroughly under running cold water. Rub with salt, scald with boiling water, then rinse again under running cold water. Put in a large pot, cover with salted water, and boil covered for 1 hour. Drain. Rinse thoroughly in cold water again. Start with clean salted water and boil tripe until almost tender. 1-2 hours.
Cook tripe with carrots, celery and onion in chicken broth until tripe
and vegetables are tender, 30-40 minutes. Remove tripe and vegetables, reserve the broth.

Melt butter in a saucepan. Stir in flour to make a smooth paste. Cook and stir until golden. Add garlic, paprika, marjoram, allspice, pepper and ginger. Brown mixture lightly. Add the broth, simmer 10 minutes, strain.
Cut tripe in 2" long thin strips, slice vegetables, stir into soup. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

• • 1-1/2 quarts water
  • • 3 medium potatoes, peeled, cut in cubes
  • • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • • 4 cloves garlic, pressed
  • • 1/2 teaspoon each of caraway seeds, and marjoram
  • • 2 tablespoons butter
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • 1 cup fresh mushrooms, sliced lengthwise, sautéed in butter
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • salt and pepper
In a large saucepot combine potatoes, salt, caraway seeds, marjoram, water. Cook 20 minutes, or until potatoes are crisp-tender.

Sauté onion and garlic in butter, stir in flour, brown lightly. Add 2 cups cooking liquid from the potatoes. Bring to boiling, cook and stir 5 minutes. Strain mixture into potatoes. Simmer 10 minutes, add mushrooms and parsley. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

• • 2 quarts milk
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 1/4 cup sugar
  • • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • • toasts or croutons

Lightly beat egg yolks in one cup milk. Pour remaining milk in a saucepot, add sugar and salt. Set over medium/low heat, bring to boiling, stirring constantly. Blend in yolks/milk mixture, heat through, but do not boil. Serve with toasts or croutons.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan, set over medium heat. Beat at low speed until soup starts to boil. Serve with toasts or crackers.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan, set over medium heat. Beat at low speed until soup is hot. Must not boil. Serve with French bread.

• • 1-1/2 bottles white table wine
  • • 6 egg yolks
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • toasts or crackers


  • • 1-1/2 quarts light beer
  • • 6 egg yolks
  • • 3 level tablespoons sugar
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • dash of cinnamon, ground clove, nutmeg
  • • French bread

Potato apple pie - Jablkový koláč bramborový
Potato plum dumplings - Švestkové knedlíky bramborové
Apple, plum, peach fritters - Jablkové, švestkové, broskvové kobližky
Fresh yeast is sold in most American supermarkets packed in 2 oz. cubes and dated for freshness (Fleischmann's, Red Star). Store it in the refrigerator but remove it at least 1 hour prior to using.

• - All ingredients as well as the pastry board or the mixing bowl must be at room temperature. Milk and butter must be lukewarm, not hot. It would inactivate the yeast. When the dough is set aside to rise it must be in a warm and draft free place. The dough should be dusted with a little flour and covered with cloth napkin.
  • - While kneading the dough, the melted butter and the salt should not touch directly the leavening, as this would retard fermentation. Therefore mix the salt with the flour and add the butter in the end when all ingredients are already mixed with the leavening.
  • - The dough for larger pieces is thicker than for small size pastries. If you find it difficult to use a wooden spoon, you can knead with hands after all ingredients are well mixed. The dough must be kneaded thoroughly, until it is smooth, feels dry, and no longer sticks to the bowl, spoon and hands.
  • - The quantities of ingredients indicated are to be followed exactly. So is the sequence of additions.
Sugar - unless otherwise indicated, i.e. crystal or confectioner's sugar, means granulated sugar.
Flour - means sifted flour. In the U.S. all flour is sold pre-sifted.
Grated lemon rind - If you do not have a manual grater, peel the lemon and chop the rind finely.
Bohemian open-faced pastries - České koláčky

• • 4 cups flour
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 2 cups milk
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 2 egg yolks
  • • dash of grated nutmeg
  • • 1 whole egg for brushing
  • • 1 cup filling or thick fruit preserve

Leavening: In a bowl stir yeast with 2 teaspoons sugar until dissolved. Add 2/3 cup flour and 1/2 cup lukewarm milk. Knead into a ball. Dust with flour, cover with napkin, let rise in a warm place. It will double in bulk within 20 minutes.
In a separate bowl combine remaining flour and sugar, lemon rind, nutmeg, salt. Place risen leavening in center.
Lightly beat egg yolks and the remaining lukewarm milk, then add it gradually to flour/leavening while mixing thoroughly. Finally add melted lukewarm butter and knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Dust with flour, cover with a napkin and let rise 40 minutes in a warm place.
Punch dough down and turn onto lightly floured pastry board. Break off dough and form balls the size of a walnut. Place them on a greased baking sheet, 4" apart. Let rise 10 minutes.

Press down the center of each ball, using bottom of a small glass or other round object, or with your fingers, so that a higher border will be formed. Brush borders with beaten egg. Spread filling evenly over center wells. Let rise 15 minutes.
(If using butter crumbs filling, brush with melted butter first. This way filling will stick).
Preheat oven to 350F, bake 15 minutes, or until borders are golden brown.

• • 4 cups coarse flour, Gold Medal Wondra
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 1-1/4 cups milk
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • dash of salt
  • • 4 tablespoons butter for brushing and for baking pan
  • • 1 cup filling

Leavening: In a bowl stir yeast with 2 teaspoons sugar until dissolved. Add 2/3 cup flour and 1/2 cup lukewarm milk. Knead into a ball. Dust with flour, cover with a napkin, set aside to rise – in a warm draft free place. It should double in bulk within 15-20 minutes.
In a separate bowl blend remaining flour with sugar, lemon rind and salt. Push to sides making a well in the center. Place risen leavening in the well.

Lightly beat egg yolks and whole egg in remaining lukewarm milk. Add it gradually to flour/leavening mixture, mixing thoroughly. Lastly, add melted lukewarm butter. Knead dough until smooth and no longer sticks to the bowl. Dust with flour, cover with napkin and let it rise 40 minutes.

Turn dough over onto a floured pastry board and roll it out to 1/3" thickness. Cut into 2 × 3" rectangles. Drop filling by teaspoonfuls on narrower side of each rectangle, roll over so that filling will be well covered with the dough. Pinch sides firmly to seal them. Dip each piece in butter, or brush on all sides with melted butter. Arrange them close together in a buttered baking pan. Let them rise 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 350F and bake 25 minutes or until golden on top. Invert 'buchty' onto a wire rack and cool, at least 20 minutes. Separate them carefully and sprinkle with sugar.

• • 8 oz. ricotta
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 2 egg yolks
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 2-3 tablespoons sponge crumbs
  • • 1 tablespoon rum
  • • 3 tablespoons golden raisins

In a bowl cream the sugar and the egg yolks. Add ricotta, lemon rind, sponge crumbs, rum and raisins - mix well. The sponge crumbs are added to thicken the filling. You can add a little more or less, to achieve the right consistency. If the filling is not thick enough, is runny, it would run out while baking and jeopardize the good look of the finished product.

• • 6 oz. ground or chopped walnuts
  • • 2/3 cup maple syrup
  • • 3/4 cup sponge crumbs
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • 2 tablespoons heavy cream

Pour the maple syrup in a saucepan and bring over medium heat. When hot, but not boiling, remove from heat, add the walnuts, vanilla sugar, lemon rind and heavy cream and as much of the sponge crumbs as needed to thicken the mixture. Mix well.

• • 3 large apples (Granny Smith)
  • • 3/4 cup sugar
  • • 1/4 cup water
  • • 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon
  • • 1 tablespoon rum
  • • 3 oz. ground or chopped almonds
  • • 1/2 cup sponge crumbs

Peel, core and quarter the apples. In a saucepan combine apples and water and simmer until soft. Purée the apples in a bowl, and mix in all remaining ingredients. To attain the desired thickness, add some of the sponge crumbs.
In a saucepan melt butter, add flour, sugar and vanilla sugar and stir until the mixture crumbles. Cool.

• • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1·1/2 cups flour
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar

• • 1 cup ground or pounded poppy seeds
  • • 1 cup milk
  • • 2/3 cup sugar
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 tablespoons golden raisins
  • • 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
In a saucepan combine poppy seeds and milk. Cook over medium/low heat, stirring often, until poppy seeds are mashed, 10-15 minutes. Add all remaining ingredients. Mix thoroughly. Cool.
⇒ A thick fruit preserve may also be used to fill "Buchty" and "Koláčky".

• • 4 cups coarse flour, Gold Medal Wondra
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 1-1/4 cups milk
  • • 1/2 cup sugar
  • • 4 egg yolks
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • dash of salt
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 4 tablespoons butter for baking pan and brushing

• • 2 cups milk, or light cream
  • • 4 egg yolks
  • • 1/2 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • 1 tablespoon corn starch

• • 1 cup white table wine
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • dash of cinnamon
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon

Prepare dough in the same manner as in Bohemian muffins. Roll it out to 1/3" thickness. Using a cookie cutter or a glass 1" in diameter cut out round cakes and lay them tightly together in a buttered baking pan. Brush sides and top with melted butter. Let rise 30 minutes in a warm place. Preheat oven to 350F, bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown on top.
Serve warm with vanilla sauce or wine froth.

In a saucepan cream egg yolks, sugar mixed with vanilla sugar, corn starch. Gradually add hot milk or cream, stirring constantly. Set over low heat, bring to boiling, stirring steadily until desired thickness is reached. Sauce should be medium thick. Strain, serve warm.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan. Set over low heat, beat with a wire whisk or electric mixer at low speed until mixture thickens and foams. Serve warm.

• • 1 lb. flour
  • • 1 cup milk
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 whole eggs
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • dash of salt
  • • 1 egg yolk to brush the loaf with
  • • grease for baking sheet

Dissolve the yeast by mixing it with a teaspoon of sugar. Add three tablespoons of flour and 1/4 cup lukewarm milk; knead the leavening into a small ball. Let it rise 20 minutes, it should double in size.

Place the remaining flour in a bowl, add eggs, lemon rind, remaining sugar, salt and milk, mix well. Finally add melted or softened butter. Knead the dough until it becames smooth and dry and no longer sticks to the bowl. Let it rise 30 minutes.

Turn the dough onto a floured pastry board and roll it out into 1/8" thick rectangle. Cover evenly with poppy seed filling and roll it into a long narrow loaf (16-17" long). Place loaf on a greased baking sheet and let rise 10 minutes. Brush with lightly beaten egg yolk and bake 20-25 minutes in 35OF oven. When cooled, cut in 3/4" slices and serve.

Leavening: In a bowl stir yeast with 2 teaspoons sugar until liquefied. Add 1 cup flour and 3/4 cup milk. Mix thoroughly. Knead into a smooth neat ball. Dust with flour, cover with a napkin and let rise 20 minutes. It should double in bulk.

In a separate bowl cream egg yolks and vanilla sugar. Gradually adding heavy cream beat at low speed until foamy. Blend in remaining flour, salt, rum, orange juice and risen leavening. Mix thoroughly. Knead into a smooth, dry, elastic dough. Let rise 30 minutes.

• • 3 cups flour
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 6 egg yolks
  • • 3/4 cup heavy cream
  • • 3/4 cup milk
  • • 1/3 cup sugar mixed with vanilla sugar
  • • 1 tablespoon rum
  • • 1 tablespoon orange juice
  • • pinch of salt
  • • 3/4 cup thick fruit preserve
  • • 2 cups oil for frying
Punch dough down, turn onto a floured pastry board and roll out to 1/3" thickness.
Using a cookie cutter or a small cup, cut out round cakes, about 2-1/2" in diameter.

Drop fruit preserve by teaspoonfuls in center of half of round cakes. Top each with a plain round cake. Press borders firmly together. Be sure they are well sealed to prevent the filling from leaking out. With a smaller round cutter cut out the final shape of the doughnuts. Put doughnuts on lightly floured board, cover with a large napkin, let rest 20 minutes. Fry in hot oil, starting with top side down, in a covered frying pan. When bottom is golden brown turn them over and finish frying, uncovered. Drain on a sieve or paper towel. When cooled, sprinkle with sugar.

• • 4 cups flour
  • • 1-1/2 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 1-1/2 cups milk
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/3 cups sugar
  • • 1 tablespoon rum
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • dash of salt
  • • 1-1/2 cups oil for frying

• • 1 cup plum or blueberry jam
  • • 1/2 cup crumbled farmer's cheese
  • • 1/2 cup sour cream
Prepare dough in the same manner as in Czech doughnuts, Roll it out to 1/3" thickness. Cut out 3" round cakes. Let rise 30 minutes, in a warm place.
Just before frying make an indentation with teaspoon or finger in center of each cake. For frying, follow directions in Czech doughnuts recipe.
Optional: Spread jam over each depression, sprinkle with crumbled farmer's cheese, dot with sour cream.

• • 1-1/2 lbs. flour
  • • 1-3/4 cups milk
  • • 1-1/2 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 2/3 cup sugar
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 10 tablespoons melted butter
  • • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • • 1 tablespoon vanilla sugar
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 10 oz. chopped almonds
  • • grease for baking pan
  • • 1 cup sugar mixed with vanilla sugar for dusting

Leavening: in a bowl stir yeast with 2 teaspoons sugar until liquefied. Add 3/4 cup flour and 3/4 cup lukewarm milk. Mix thoroughly, knead, form a ball. Dust lightly with flour, cover with a napkin. Let rise 30 minutes, or until doubled in bulk.

Place all remaining ingredients and the risen leavening on a floured pastry board, knead with the palms of your hands, until dough feels smooth, dry and elastic. Sprinkle with flour, cover with napkin, let rise 40 minutes.
Punch dough down, shape into a loaf and transfer into a buttered and floured loaf pan. Let rise 15 minutes. Preheat oven to 350F, bake 30 minutes, or until top is golden.
Next day: Cut loaf into 1/3" thick slices. Dredge each slice in sugar mixed with vanilla sugar, shake off excess. Put them on a clean dry baking sheet, brown lightly on both sides in 250-300F oven.
Biscuits keep fresh for many weeks in an airtight tin.
Preparation time: 2 hours 30 minutes, plus 30 minutes next day

• • 4 cups flour
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/2 cup sugar
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 2 egg yolks
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • grated rind of one lemon
  • • dash of salt
  • • 1 cup milk
  • • 1/2 cup golden raisins
  • • 1/2 cup slivered almonds
  • • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • • 1 egg for brushing, butter for baking tray

Leavening: In a bowl stir the yeast and 2 teaspoons sugar until the yeast dissolves. Add 1/2 cup flour and one third of the milk and knead it into a ball. Sprinkle with flour and set aside to rise, in a warm, draft free area. It will double in bulk within 20 minutes.

In a separate bowl combine the remaining flour, sugar, salt and lemon rind. Make a well in the center and place the risen leavening, egg yolks and whole egg in it. Gradually adding the remaining milk, mix well. Lastly add raisins and melted butter and knead with a wooden spoon, or with hands, until dough is smooth and no longer sticks to the bowl. Set aside, dust with flour and let rise 30 minutes. Punch dough down, let rise 30 minutes again.

After the dough has risen at the second time, turn it over a floured pastry board and divide in two halves. Shape each into a ball. Place on a baking tray lined with buttered wax paper. Let rise 30 minutes. Brush with lightly beaten egg. With a sharp knife slit the top of each bread cross-wise. Let rise 10 minutes. Preheat oven to 350°F. Sprinkle with slivered almonds and bake 30-35 minutes or until breads are golden brown. Dust with sugar and cool at room temperature.

Prepare the dough exactly as for Easter braid. After it has risen twice, turn it out onto a floured pastry board and divide in three identical sections. Roll and stretch each section into a rope 25" long. Press together both ends of each rope twist it so that it will be braided and make a loop at the end. Place a raw egg in each loop. Place braids on an oven tray lined with buttered wax paper, let them rise 20 minutes. Brush with lightly beaten egg and bake 30 minutes in 350 F preheated oven.

• • 1 lb. flour
  • • 1 cup milk
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 6 egg yolks
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/2 cup golden raisins
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • dash of salt
  • • 1 beaten egg for brushing
  • • 3 tablespoons sugar mixed with vanilla sugar for dusting
• • 1/3 cup slivered almonds to sprinkle over loaf before baking
Leavening: In a bowl stir yeast and 2 teaspoons sugar until dissolved. Add 1/2 cup flour and 1/3 cup lukewarm milk. Knead into a ball, dust with flour, let rise 20-30 minutes, until doubled in bulk.

In a separate bowl combine remaining flour, sugar, salt, lemon rind. Make a well in center. Put egg yolks and risen leavening in the well. Gradually adding remaining lukewarm milk, mix thoroughly. Add raisins and melted butter, knead dough until smooth, dry and elastic. Dust with flour, let rise 30 minutes.
Punch dough down, let rise again 30 minutes.
Turn dough over onto a lightly floured pastry board, divide in two halves.

Divide one half into 3 identical sections. Form 3 ropes 13" long. Braid them, pinch together both ends. Place on oven tray lined with buttered wax paper. Make a shallow indentation in center lengthwise,

then brush depression lightly with a beaten egg white.
Divide remaining dough into 5 identical sections. Form 5 ropes 13" long. Braid 3 ropes and place on top of the thicker braid. Again make indentation in center and brush with beaten egg white.
Braid last two ropes, place on top of second layer. Press each end firmly together. Let loaf rise 30 minutes. Brush with beaten egg.

Preheat oven to 375F. Bake 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350F, bake 20-25 minutes, check with wooden pick for doneness. Dust with sugar mixed with vanilla sugar while hot. Cool at room temperature at least 1 hour. Slice.

• • 1-1/4 cups flour
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • 6 egg yolks
  • • 2/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • • 1/2 cup diced dried apricots, other dry fruit can substitute
  • • 1/4 cup slivered almonds
  • • 1/2 cup golden raisins
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • grated rind of one lemon

In a saucepan combine the egg yolks, the egg, sugar and lemon rind and set over medium/low heat. Beat until the mixture is lukewarm. Remove from heat and continue beating until cool and creamy. Fold in the flour mixed with baking powder, dried apricots, almonds, raisins. Lastly, add melted butter. Turn the batter into a buttered oblong loaf pan lined with wax paper. Bake 30 minutes at 350F. Test for doneness with a cake tester or toothpick. Inserting it in the center, it should come out clean. Let stand for 5 minutes before turning the bread out onto a cake rack. Dust lightly with sugar. Cool and slice.
Optional: Spread apricot jelly very thinly over the bread and top with sugar icing. When cooled, or when the icing hardens (approximately 2 hours), slice.

• • apricot jelly
  • • 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar
  • • 6 teaspoons water

Mix sugar and water well and cover the cake evenly. If the icing is too thick, add water. It should be somewhat thick, not too runny. For variety: replace 3 teaspoons of water with 3 teaspoons of lemon juice, coffee, rum or any other juice to add taste and color. The cake must be warm while frosting it in order to achieve a glossy look. Using hot water or milk you will get a fondant-like look.

• • 1 cup flour
  • • 1 cup sugar
  • • 1 cup ground walnuts
  • • 3/4 cup sponge crumbs, or bread crumbs
  • • 2 eggs, whole
  • • 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon
  • • 1/4 cup golden raisins
  • • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • • butter and flour for baking pan
  • • 10 walnut or pecan halves for decorating
  • • 3/4 cup sugar icing

• • 2·1/2 cups flour
  • • 1 cup sugar
  • • 10 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 eggs, separated
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 2 teaspoons vanilla sugar
  • • 2·1/2 teaspoons baking powder
  • • 2/3 cup milk
  • • 1 lb. cherries (preferably Morello cherries)
  • • butter or margarine and flour for baking dish
  • • sugar for dusting

Beat the whole eggs until they are foamy, adding the sugar gradually. Stir in all ingredients, leaving the flour mixed with baking powder to be added last. Turn the batter into a buttered and floured loaf pan and bake at 350F 40-45 minutes, or until the toothpick comes out clean. When done, invert the bread onto a cake rack, cover with icing and decorate with walnut or pecan halves.
Sugar icing: Same as used on fruit cake.
Instead of icing and decorating with nuts, just dust it with sugar mixed with a pinch of cinnamon.

Beat two egg whites and half of the sugar until stiff, set aside. In a bowl combine the butter, the egg yolks and the remaining sugar and beat until creamy and fluffy. Add lemon rind, vanilla sugar and milk, mix well. Fold in the beaten egg whites by spoonfuls, mixing gently after each addition. Fold in the flour mixed with baking powder. Pour the batter into a buttered and floured baking dish – fill no more than half full. Spread the cherries evenly over the batter and bake at 375F for 30 minutes, or until golden on top. Remove from oven, cool, cut into squares, dust with sugar.

In a bowl combine all dry ingredients, mix them, add the lemon rind and the milk. Mix thoroughly and pour the batter into a greased and floured baking dish. Bake in preheated 350F oven about 45 minutes. Cool, cut into squares and dust with sugar.
Blend baking powder and flour. Add sugar, egg yolk, lemon rind, salt, milk and butter. Mix thoroughly and knead until smooth, about 10 minutes.

On a greased oven tray roll dough out to 1/3" thickness, leaving the edges a little higher. Mix apples, raisins, sugar-cinnamon and spread evenly over dough. Bake at 350F, 20-25 minutes, until border is golden brown. Place pie on a wire rack to cool, dust with sugar mixed with vanilla sugar. Cut into squares.
Instead of one oblong pie, you can make two smaller round pies.

  • • 1·1/2 cups ground or pounded poppy seeds
  • • 2 cups cornstarch
  • • 1 package (1/2 oz.) baking powder

  • • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 6 tablespoons butter, softened
  • • 2/3 cup milk
  • • 1 egg yolk
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • pinch of salt

  • • 2 tablespoons sugar mixed with vanilla sugar

  • • 1/3 cup golden raisins
  • • 3 tablespoons sugar mixed with 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon

• • 1-1/2 cups flour
  • • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • • 2 medium potatoes, boiled, mashed
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 egg
  • • grease for baking dish

• • 1/2 cup hazelnuts or walnuts, ground or chopped
  • • 3 medium apples, Granny Smith, peeled, thinly sliced parboiled
  • • 2/3 cup sugar

Blend baking powder into flour. Add all ingredients and mix thoroughly. Knead about 10 minutes, until dough is smooth and dry.
